messages.content: What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?

function.name: entropy_change_calculate
function.description: Calculate the change in entropy for a mass of a specific substance under set initial and final conditions. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which the change in entropy is calculated.

mass.description: The mass of the substance in kg.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the substance in degree Celsius.

pressure.description: The pressure the substance is under in atmospheres.

message.reasoning: We need to calculate entropy change for heating ice from 0°C to 100°C under 1 atm. But ice at 0°C to water at 0°C? Actually heating ice at 0°C to 100°C: first melt ice at 0°C to water at 0°C, then heat water from 0°C to 100°C. Also need to consider latent heat of fusion. Also need to consider specific heat capacities: ice cp ~ 2.09 kJ/kg·K, water cp ~ 4.18 kJ/kg·K. Latent heat of fusion Lf ~ 334 kJ/kg. So entropy change ΔS = ∫ dQ_rev/T. For melting at constant T=0°C (273.15 K): ΔS_melt = Lf / T = 334000 J/kg / 273.15 K ≈ 1222 J/K. Then heating water from 273.15 K to 373.15 K: ΔS_heat = ∫ cp dT / T = cp * ln(Tf/Ti). cp water = 4180 J/kg·K. So ΔS_water = 4180 * ln(373.15/273.15) ≈ 4180 * ln(1.366) ≈ 4180 * 0.312 = 1305 J/K. Total ΔS = 1222 + 1305 = 2527 J/K. But also heating ice from 0°C to 0°C? No. So answer ~ 2.53 kJ/K. Provide explanation. Use function? The user asked "What is the change in entropy in Joules per Kelvin of a 1kg ice block at 0°C if it is heated to 100°C under 1 atmosphere of pressure?" We can compute using function.
